raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Adds [Recursive's Flint](https://huggingface.co/RecursiveSI/flint), a MoE model with 40B total and 2.5B active parameters, with day-0 support for both released checkpoints:
- `RecursiveSI/flint`: BF16 safetensors;
- `RecursiveSI/flint-nvfp4-gguf`: an NVFP4 GGUF, served weight-only (W4A16).

The model lives in `vllm/models/flint/`, together with Flint-specific kernels for small-batch decode on a single Blackwell GPU.

## Claims

- **Architecture:** 49 layers.
  - Attention: 35 layers use a 513-token sliding window with RoPE; 14 use full attention with no positional encoding. All layers use GQA (32 query / 4 KV heads, head dim 128), per-head Q/K RMSNorm and learned attention sinks.
  - MoE: 256 experts with sigmoid top-6 routing and renormalized weights, plus a shared expert. Layers 0–1 are dense.
  - Context: 262K tokens. The untied LM head produces FP32 logits.
- **NVFP4 GGUF:**
  - Each 64-value superblock is 4 × (UE4M3 scale + 16 E2M1 codes), with an FP32 scale per tensor (per expert for MoE weights). It is repacked losslessly at load into the ModelOpt NVFP4 layout and runs on the existing W4A16 kernels.
  - Config and tokenizer come from the BF16 repo (`--hf-config-path`, `--tokenizer`).
  - It loads by HF repo ID or local path, and needs `gguf>=0.19.0`.
- **Numerics:** the kernels follow the reference implementation's rounding points.
  - FP32 fused add + RMSNorm, rounded once.
  - FP32 gate/up for the routed experts.
  - Exact SiLU after BF16 rounding for the shared expert.
  - FP32 RoPE table, BF16 router logits.
- **Speed:** single-GPU (TP=1) forward time on GB200 with 100K tokens of context, from `vllm bench forward`.

  | | stock vLLM layers | this PR |
  |:---|---:|---:|
  | NVFP4 decode, batch 1 | 4.81 ms | **1.78 ms** (2.7×) |
  | NVFP4 decode, batch 8 | 8.24 ms | 5.70 ms (1.45×) |
  | NVFP4 prefill, 8K tokens | 206.6 ms | 144.6 ms (1.43×) |
  | BF16 decode, batch 1 | 3.53 ms | 2.34 ms (1.51×) |

  Served end to end, batch-1 NVFP4 decode at 100K context takes 2.06 ms per token (about 485 tokens/s).
- **Kernels:**
  - fused Q/K norm + RoPE + KV-cache write (Triton);
  - small-batch MoE: a GEMV router with fused top-k, plus expert-indexed GEMVs, with FlashInfer's CuTe DSL W4A16 grouped GEMM for larger batches;
  - a small-batch NVFP4/BF16 dense GEMV (CuTe DSL) on the same packed weights;
  - norm and SiLU kernels with the reference's rounding;
  - CuTe DSL split-KV decode attention with sinks and sliding windows;
  - for up to 8 decode requests, a 7-kernel-per-layer path chained with programmatic dependent launch (346 kernels per forward instead of 1,096).
- **Fallback:** other configurations use vLLM's standard layers: TP > 1, EP, and GPUs outside the SM100 family such as sm_120.
- **Serving:** tool calling and reasoning use the existing `glm47` parsers; see the recipe in `recipes/models/RecursiveSI/flint.yaml`.

## Validation

Accuracy was measured on the development branch, which has the same model code as this PR, on one GB200 with the default sampling settings (temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95, top-k 20):

| Eval | BF16 | NVFP4 |
|:---|---:|---:|
| GSM8K (1,319, chat, 16K max tokens) | 0.950 | 0.950 |
| GPQA-Diamond (198 × 4) | 0.721 | 0.696 |
| MRCR (48 samples, up to 114K-token prompts; mean of 3 runs) | 0.47 | 0.46 |
| Tool-calling suite (19 cases × 10 runs) | 10/10 every case | 10/10 every case |

- **Logit agreement:** prompt-logprob KL against an FP32 reference forward pass stays at the level of the stock-layer implementation: 0.21 / 0.04 / 0.11 for BF16 and 0.13 / 0.03 / 0.06 for NVFP4, over 2–6K-token prompts. The model is ill-conditioned in BF16; an independent BF16 implementation agrees with FP32 on only 90–96% of top-1 tokens. This KL criterion is therefore used instead of bitwise comparison.
- **Unit tests:** `tests/models/flint/` covers each kernel against a reference implementation, plus the GGUF repack. It runs in one new B200 CI step.
- **This PR's tree** (one GB200, default settings, both checkpoints from their public HF repo IDs). Details are in the first comment.
  - GSM8K: NVFP4 0.947, BF16 0.954.
  - Tool-call suite: 10/10 on every case for both checkpoints.
  - Forward time matches the development branch: NVFP4 decode batch 1 1.78 ms, batch 8 5.70 ms, 8K prefill 144.4 ms; BF16 2.34 / 6.83 / 145.9 ms.
  - `pytest tests/models/flint`: 165 passed, 1 skipped.

```bash
pytest tests/models/flint
vllm serve RecursiveSI/flint-nvfp4-gguf --hf-config-path RecursiveSI/flint --tokenizer RecursiveSI/flint \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser glm47 --reasoning-parser glm47 --exclude-tools-when-tool-choice-none
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --use-chat-completions --max-tokens 16384
vllm bench forward --model RecursiveSI/flint-nvfp4-gguf --hf-config-path RecursiveSI/flint --tokenizer RecursiveSI/flint \
  --load-format auto --max-model-len 110000 --kv-len-jitter 0 --case d1=1*1@100000 --case d8=8*1@100000 --case p8k=8192@100000
```

## Details

- **Changes to shared code:**
  - registry entries (model, config, test registry);
  - one docs row;
  - `docker/Dockerfile`: installs `gguf>=0.19.0` in the `vllm-openai` image, so the NVFP4 GGUF checkpoint loads out of the box.
  - `maybe_override_with_speculators`: skips speculators detection for a single local file, so a `.gguf` path can be passed as `--model`.
- **No torch.compile:** the model runs eagerly, and decode runs under CUDA graphs.
- **Rust frontend:** not supported yet for this recipe. It rejects `--exclude-tools-when-tool-choice-none`, `--hf-config-path` and `--tokenizer`; the recipe sets `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=0`.
- **Known limitations:** prefill for short prompts is CPU-bound by eager kernel launches. Batch-1 decode time varies by a few percent between processes; this is GPU state, not configuration.
- **Not a duplicate:** no other open or closed vLLM PR or issue covers Flint.
- **AI assistance:** Claude Code was used to write the implementation, kernels and tests, and to run the benchmarks and evals. I reviewed the changes.

---

<details>
<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>

| Check | NVFP4 (`RecursiveSI/flint-nvfp4-gguf`) | BF16 (`RecursiveSI/flint`) |
|:---|---:|---:|
| GSM8K (1,319, chat, 16K max tokens) | 0.951 | 0.952 |
| Tool-call suite (19 cases × 10 runs) | 10/10 every case | 10/10 every case |
| Forward, decode batch 1 @ 100K | 1.78 ms | 2.34 ms |
| Forward, decode batch 8 @ 100K | 5.70 ms | 6.83 ms |
| Forward, prefill 8K @ 100K | 144.8 ms | 146.2 ms |

- **Reference (development branch):** GSM8K 0.950 / 0.950. Forward: NVFP4 1.78 / 5.70 / 144.6 ms, BF16 2.34 / 6.84 / 146.0 ms.
- **GSM8K errors:** none of the 1,319 requests errored; 1 hit the 16K output-token limit.
- **Unit tests:** `pytest tests/models/flint` gives 267 passed, 1 skipped (9.6 min on one GB200).
- **Dependencies:** FlashInfer 0.7.2, torch 2.14.0+cu130, `gguf` 0.19.0.

Thanks for the day-0 support! We brought Flint NVFP4 up on a single **RTX 5090 (sm_120)** with `vllm/vllm-openai:flint` (0.32.0rc1.dev348+ge7c846767) and hit two issues; both still reproduce against the current head of this PR (db02bc9f0).

**1. `_flint_kernels()` has no arch gate, so sm_120 fails at load**

It checks only TP=1 / quant type / EP, so on sm_120 it selects `FlintNvfp4Experts`, whose warmup goes through the CuTe-DSL grouped MoE (FlashInfer `moe_utils`, SM90/SM100 only):

```
File "vllm/models/flint/ops/moe.py", line 900, in _repack
    moe_cute.warmup(
...
File "flashinfer/compilation_context.py", line 162, in get_nvcc_flags_list
RuntimeError: No supported CUDA architectures found for major versions [9, 10].
```

Gating it on arch makes sm_120 take the stock layers, as the docstring describes (plus `from vllm.platforms import current_platform`):

```diff
 def _flint_kernels(
     quant_config: QuantizationConfig | None, parallel: ParallelConfig | None = None
 ) -> bool:
     """Flint's kernels serve the BF16 and NVFP4 checkpoints on a single GPU
-    (TP=1, and for the MoE no EP/EPLB); other configurations use vLLM's stock
-    layers."""
+    (SM90/SM100, TP=1, and for the MoE no EP/EPLB); other configurations use
+    vLLM's stock layers."""
+    if not (
+        current_platform.is_device_capability_family(90)
+        or current_platform.is_device_capability_family(100)
+    ):
+        return False
     if get_tensor_model_parallel_world_size() != 1 or not (
```

With this, the 5090 runs `MarlinNvFp4LinearKernel` + MARLIN NvFp4 MoE + FlashInfer attention. Output is coherent and needle retrieval works at 6.5K/12K tokens (well past the 513-token window). We have not run GSM8K or other accuracy evals on this path. Measured with `vllm bench serve` (random dataset, ignore_eos):

| in/out | concurrency | TTFT p50 | TPOT | output tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1024/256 | 1 | 56 ms | 3.61 ms | 262 |
| 1024/256 | 32 | 218 ms | 11.3 ms | 2,572 |
| 1024/256 | 64 | 303 ms | 20.4 ms | 2,839 |
| 16384/256 | 1 | 657 ms | 4.10 ms | 150 |

Open question: the small-batch Triton decode MoE path (≤ `DECODE_MAX_TOKENS`) might also work on sm_120 (it relies on `cvt.rn.bf16x2.e2m1x2`), which could help batch-1 decode. We haven't tested that, so the gate above turns everything off for safety.

**2. The `flint` image is missing `gguf`**

Loading `RecursiveSI/flint-nvfp4-gguf` fails with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'gguf'` from `gguf_nvfp4.py:172`. The PR description lists `gguf` 0.19.0 as a dependency, but it isn't installed in the image, and the test uses `importorskip`. Could it be added to the image, or the loader raise an error that says how to install it?

Minor: passing the `.gguf` file path itself as `--model` fails in `maybe_override_with_speculators` (it tries to parse it as JSON); passing the directory works.

Tried this on sm_120 with the NVFP4 GGUF: serving on an RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Workstation Edition, kernel tests on an RTX 5070 Ti.

`_flint_kernels()` checks TP, EP/EPLB and the quant config but not the device, so a single sm_120 GPU picks the Flint kernels, and the MoE path doesn't run there. With the module level SM100 skips removed, the flint tests give 8 failed, 235 passed on sm_120:

- `test_moe_matches_reference[7|64|600]`, `test_decode_and_grouped_paths_agree[1|6]`, `test_shared_expert_on_aux_stream[64]`: `RuntimeError: No supported CUDA architectures found for major versions [9, 10]` (FlashInfer JIT)
- `test_bf16_decode_matches_trtllm[1|12]`: `The trtllm-gen batched GEMM cubin manifest contains no kernels runnable on sm120; this backend currently ships cubins for sm100, sm103 and sm107`

Routing, dequant, the Triton decode GEMVs, `qkv_fused` and `qk_norm_rope` all pass on sm_120.

We gated it on the device:

```diff
 def _flint_kernels(quant_config, parallel=None) -> bool:
+    if not current_platform.is_device_capability_family(100):
+        return False
     if get_tensor_model_parallel_world_size() != 1 or not (
```

With that, sm_120 runs on the stock layers (Marlin W4A16 NVFP4, FlashInfer attention with sinks) and lands on Recursive's NVFP4 numbers: LiveCodeBench v6 82.2% on a 45 problem sample, SWE-bench Verified 80% on 50 tasks (mini-swe-agent, no network). The `glm47` tool call and reasoning parsers worked as in the recipe. A finer gate could keep the Triton decode path on sm_120 if you want it there.

Test log, patch and setup: https://github.com/DataCraftsmanAU/flint-independent-eval (`serving/sm120-kernel-tests.log`)

Thanks @zflowai and @DataCraftsmanAU for testing on sm_120 and for the detailed reports. Addressed in 826fd3fdca:

1. **Architecture gate.** `_flint_kernels()` now returns `False` unless `current_platform.is_device_capability_family(100)`. The Flint kernels are built and tested only on SM100 (the kernel tests already skip elsewhere), so sm_120 and other GPUs take vLLM's standard layers: Marlin W4A16 NVFP4 for linears and MoE, plus FlashInfer attention with sinks. This matches the patches you both used, and your LiveCodeBench, SWE-bench and needle results on that path are good to see. Keeping the Triton decode GEMVs on sm_120 with a finer gate is a reasonable follow-up; it needs its own accuracy and performance validation, so I'm leaving it out of this PR.
2. **`gguf` in the image.** The `vllm-openai` Dockerfile now installs `gguf>=0.19.0`, alongside the other server extras, so the NVFP4 GGUF checkpoint loads out of the box; `docker/versions.json` is regenerated. Outside Docker, the loader already raises `ImportError: ... (pip install 'gguf>=0.19.0')`.
3. **A `.gguf` file as `--model`.** `maybe_override_with_speculators` now returns early for a single local file, since a single file has no speculators config, so `--model /path/to/flint-nvfp4.gguf --hf-config-path RecursiveSI/flint --tokenizer RecursiveSI/flint` resolves. A regression test is added in `tests/transformers_utils/test_speculators_override.py`.

Tests:
- `pytest tests/transformers_utils/test_speculators_override.py tests/models/flint/test_gguf_nvfp4.py`: 24 passed, 1 skipped.
- On GB200, the Flint kernels are still selected: NVFP4 forward, decode batch 1 / batch 8 at 100K context = 1.78 / 5.70 ms, unchanged.

**Simplified the Flint code: −198 lines, now 7,534 added. No change in behavior or speed.** Commits `4a1c5980a9`..`aed08d76a6`.

- **GEMV:** the row-load and reduction helpers that `nvfp4_gemv` and `moe_gemv` both had are now shared in `cute_primitives`. Removed the GEMV fallbacks for untuned shapes and tiles, which the model never reaches. One dequant-GEMM threshold replaces a per-shape table.
- **MoE:**
  - Weight preparation now uses vLLM's FlashInfer CuTe DSL helpers (`reorder_w13_to_w31_for_flashinfer_cutedsl`, `interleave_linear_and_gate`, `swizzle_blockscale`); the prepared tensors are bitwise identical to before.
  - Removed the unreachable no-shared-expert paths.
  - The two router GEMV kernels are now one, with a `FUSE_NORM` flag.
- **Attention:** uses `cute_primitives.mma` instead of a duplicate wrapper, has one `o_proj` tail, and drops some always-true guards.
- **Model, CI and recipe:**
  - `FlintForCausalLM` no longer implements `MixtureOfExperts`; it was used only for EPLB, which Flint doesn't support.
  - Removed the unused `head_dtype` config field.
  - The Flint tests now run in one B200 step (the CPU step is removed).
  - The recipe no longer sets `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND`.
- **Tests:** trimmed redundant cases.

**Tried and rejected**, each measured A/B on GB200:

| Change | Result |
|:---|:---|
| FlashInfer's public `launch_w4a16_moe` (unfused shared-expert add) | NVFP4 decode at batch 8 is 1.7% slower |
| Drop the Triton NVFP4 GEMV MoE tier at 3–6 tokens | Batch 3 is 9% slower and batch 4 7% slower |
| `skinny_gemm` for the BF16 dense GEMV | BF16 decode at batch 4–16 is 2–6% slower |

**Validation on `aed08d76a6`** (one GB200, default settings, both checkpoints from their public HF repo IDs):

| Check | NVFP4 | BF16 |
|:---|---:|---:|
| GSM8K (1,319) | 0.947 | 0.954 |
| Tool-call suite (19 cases × 10 runs) | 10/10 every case | 10/10 every case |
| Forward, decode batch 1 / batch 8 / 8K prefill @ 100K | 1.78 / 5.70 / 144.4 ms | 2.34 / 6.83 / 145.9 ms |

- `pytest tests/models/flint`: 165 passed, 1 skipped.
- The forward times match the earlier run.
- GSM8K runs at temperature 1.0, so it varies by about ±0.5 pp between runs; the MoE outputs are bitwise identical before and after the cleanup.

**CI fix (`6d3d1dfd89`):** the Flint B200 step failed with `ptxas error: Unexpected instruction types specified for 'cvt'` in the Triton NVFP4 MoE decode kernels.

**Cause.** `cvt.rn.bf16x2.e2m1x2` needs PTX ISA 9.2, which means ptxas 13.2 or newer. The CI image builds Triton from source, and that Triton uses the image's system ptxas from CUDA 13.0. The Triton wheel instead bundles a CUDA 13.3 `ptxas-blackwell`, which is why the tests passed locally. The CuTe DSL kernels use the same instruction but bring their own ptxas.

**Fix.** At import, `moe.py` checks which ptxas Triton will use for Blackwell (`get_ptxas(100).version`):
- **ptxas 13.2 or newer:** the decode keeps the BF16 form, so speed and outputs are unchanged.
- **Older ptxas:** it uses `cvt.rn.f16x2.e2m1x2` and an FP16 multiply. Every E2M1 × E4M3 product is exact in FP16 too. The exhaustive `test_dequant_exact` covers whichever form is active.

**Validation** (one GB200):
- `pytest tests/models/flint`: 165 passed, 1 skipped, both with CI's CUDA 13.0 ptxas (`TRITON_PTXAS_BLACKWELL_PATH`, FP16 path) and with the default ptxas (BF16 path).
- NVFP4 decode at batch 1/3/4/6, A/B on the same GPU: unchanged (within ±0.05%).
- An FP16-only version was 2–3% slower at batch 3–6, because widening FP16 to FP32 costs an instruction per element. That's why the BF16 path stays where ptxas supports it.

The other two failures are unrelated to this PR:
- `test_gptoss_mxfp4mxfp8_moe_flashinfer_cutlass`: the server could not start (`OSError: [Errno 98] Address already in use`).
- `test_w4a16_machete_bfloat16_deterministic`: a Machete nondeterminism check, which this PR does not touch.

**AMD CI (`fc3b190acf`).**

- **`amd-mi355-basic-models-other`:** `test_registry_imports[FlintForCausalLM]` failed with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'flashinfer'`. The Flint model imported FlashInfer's attention backend and the CuTe DSL decode-attention kernel at module level, and ROCm has neither. Both are now imported where the model is built, and only on the Flint-kernel path for the CuTe DSL kernel. Checked that `vllm.models.flint.model` imports with `flashinfer` and `cutlass` unavailable. On GB200: `pytest tests/models/flint` gives 165 passed, 1 skipped, and NVFP4 decode is unchanged (batch 1: 1.78 ms, batch 8: 5.71 ms).
- **`amd-mi300-push-nixlconnector-pp-prefill-pd-accuracy`:** unrelated. Worker startup fails in `deepseek-vl2-tiny`'s timm vision tower with `RuntimeError: Tensor.item() cannot be called on meta tensors`.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

  - `docker/Dockerfile`: installs `gguf>=0.19.0` in the `vllm-openai` image, so the NVFP4 GGUF checkpoint loads out of the box.
  - `maybe_override_with_speculators`: skips speculators detection for a single local file, so a `.gguf` path can be passed as `--model`.
- **No torch.compile:** the model runs eagerly, and decode runs under CUDA graphs.
- **Rust frontend:** not supported yet for this recipe. It rejects `--exclude-tools-when-tool-choice-none`, `--hf-config-path` and `--tokenizer`; the recipe sets `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=0`.
- **Known limitations:** prefill for short prompts is CPU-bound by eager kernel launches. Batch-1 decode time varies by a few percent between processes; this is GPU state, not configuration.
- **Not a duplicate:** no other open or closed vLLM PR or issue covers Flint.
- **AI assistance:** Claude Code was used to write the implementation, kernels and tests, and to run the benchmarks and evals. I reviewed the changes.

+# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://recipes.vllm.ai/recipe.schema.json
+
+meta:
+  title: "Flint"
+  slug: "flint"
+  provider: "RecursiveSI"
+  description: "39.8B-parameter (2.5B active) MoE with hybrid sliding-window / full attention, reasoning and tool calling; BF16 and NVFP4 checkpoints on a single Blackwell GPU."
+  date_added: 2026-10-18
+  date_updated: 2026-10-21
+  tasks:
+    - text
+  performance_headline: "Single GB200, NVFP4: ~2.0 ms per output token at batch 1 with 100K context"
+  related_recipes: []
+  default_hardware: gb200
+  hardware:
+    gb200: verified
+
+model:
+  model_id: "RecursiveSI/flint"
+  min_vllm_version: "nightly"
+  install:
+    pip:
+      note: "Use a nightly wheel. The NVFP4 GGUF checkpoint also needs `pip install 'gguf>=0.19.0'`."
+    docker:
+      note: "Use the vLLM nightly image."
+  architecture: moe
+  parameter_count: "39.8B"
+  active_parameters: "2.5B"
+  context_length: 262144
+  base_args: []
+  base_env: {}
+  rust_frontend: unsupported
+
+features:
+  tool_calling:
+    description: "Automatic tool choice with the GLM-4.7 XML tool-call parser (Flint's chat template emits <tool_call>/<arg_key>/<arg_value>); tools are dropped from the prompt when tool_choice is none, as in the reference runtime."
+    args: ["--enable-auto-tool-choice", "--tool-call-parser", "glm47", "--exclude-tools-when-tool-choice-none"]
+  reasoning:
+    description: "Return the <think>…</think> block in the reasoning field; the model decides per turn whether to reason."
+    args: ["--reasoning-parser", "glm47"]
+
+opt_in_features: []
+
+variants:
+  default:
+    precision: bf16
+    vram_minimum_gb: 96
+    description: "BF16 safetensors (79.6 GB of weights)."
+  nvfp4:
+    model_id: "RecursiveSI/flint-nvfp4-gguf"
+    precision: nvfp4
+    vram_minimum_gb: 29
+    description: "NVFP4 GGUF served weight-only (W4A16); 23.5 GB resident after load (the LM head is dequantized to BF16). Config and tokenizer come from the BF16 repo."
+    extra_args: ["--hf-config-path", "RecursiveSI/flint", "--tokenizer", "RecursiveSI/flint"]
+
+compatible_strategies:
+  - single_node_tp
+
+hardware_overrides: {}
+
+strategy_overrides:
+  single_node_tp:
+    tp: 1
+
+guide: |
+  ## Overview
+
+  Flint is a 39.8B-parameter mixture-of-experts model (256 experts, top-6 sigmoid routing plus a
+  shared expert; ~2.5B parameters active per token) with 49 layers: 35 sliding-window layers
+  (window 513, RoPE) and 14 full-attention layers (no RoPE), GQA 32/4, attention sinks, and a
+  262,144-token context. Two checkpoints are served:
+
+  - [RecursiveSI/flint](https://huggingface.co/RecursiveSI/flint): BF16 safetensors.
+  - [RecursiveSI/flint-nvfp4-gguf](https://huggingface.co/RecursiveSI/flint-nvfp4-gguf): a single
+    NVFP4 GGUF (repacked losslessly at load and run as W4A16, like the reference runtime). It ships
+    no config or tokenizer; both come from the BF16 repo.
+
+  Tested end to end on one GB200 (TP=1, BF16 KV cache, CUDA graphs, no torch.compile) for both
+  checkpoints. On a single GPU the Flint kernels are always used (fused MoE, small-batch CuTe GEMV,
+  CuTe decode attention, low-latency decode path for <= 8 requests); TP > 1 and expert parallelism
+  fall back to stock vLLM layers and are not validated.
+
+  ## Launch
+
+  BF16:
+
+  ```bash
+  vllm serve RecursiveSI/flint --served-model-name flint \
+    --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser glm47 --reasoning-parser glm47 \
+    --exclude-tools-when-tool-choice-none
+  ```
+
+  NVFP4 (requires `gguf>=0.19.0`):
+
+  ```bash
+  vllm serve RecursiveSI/flint-nvfp4-gguf \
+    --hf-config-path RecursiveSI/flint --tokenizer RecursiveSI/flint \
+    --served-model-name flint \
+    --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser glm47 --reasoning-parser glm47 \
+    --exclude-tools-when-tool-choice-none
+  ```
+
+  ## Client usage
+
+  Use `/v1/chat/completions`. Sampling defaults from `generation_config.json`: temperature 1.0,
+  top_p 0.95, top_k 20 (greedy decoding is not validated). Reasoning is returned in `reasoning`
+  and counts toward `max_tokens`; use `max_tokens` of at least 32768 for hard problems.
+
+  ```bash
+  curl localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
+    "model": "flint",
+    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "What is 17*23? Answer briefly."}],
+    "max_tokens": 1024
+  }'
+  ```
+
+  Accuracy on GB200 with this recipe (BF16 / NVFP4): GSM8K 0.950 / 0.950, GPQA-Diamond (4 repeats)
+  0.721 / 0.696, MRCR (48 samples, up to 114K-token prompts) ~0.47 / ~0.46, tool-calling suite
+  (19 cases x 10: typed args, tool selection, parallel calls, multi-turn, tool_choice none,
+  escaping, streaming) 10/10 on every case.
+
+  ## Benchmarking
+
+  Forward time on one GB200 (`vllm bench forward`, batch x context, us):
+
+  | shape | BF16 | NVFP4 |
+  |---|---|---|
+  | decode 1 x 100K | 2341 | 1783 |
+  | decode 8 x 100K | 6836 | 5703 |
+  | decode 32 x 100K | 19580 | 16716 |
+  | prefill 8K @ 100K | 145617 | 144765 |
+
+  Serving (NVFP4, `vllm bench serve`, random 1000 in / 1000 out): TPOT 2.0 ms at concurrency 1,
+  2.8 ms at 8, 4.9 ms at 32, 8.5 ms at 128; median inter-token latency 2.06 ms at batch 1 with
+  100K context. Prefill runs eagerly and is CPU-bound on kernel-launch overhead: TTFT is ~60 ms
+  for a short prompt and ~125 ms for an 8K-token prompt.
+
+  ## Troubleshooting
+
+  - Rust frontend: not supported for this recipe. It rejects `--exclude-tools-when-tool-choice-none`,
+    and for NVFP4 also `--hf-config-path` / `--tokenizer`; keep the default Python frontend.
+  - Reasoning parser: the reference runtime's `deepseek-v3` name maps to vLLM's `deepseek_v3`
+    parser, which only extracts reasoning when the request enables `thinking`; with Flint the
+    reasoning then stays in `content`. Use `glm47`.
+  - If `content` contains literal `<think>` or `<tool_call>` text, the server was started without
+    the parsers above.
+  - Batch-1 decode time varies by ~3-4% between sessions (a GPU-side state, not configuration).
+
+  ## References
+
+  - [Flint (BF16) model card](https://huggingface.co/RecursiveSI/flint)
+  - [Flint NVFP4 model card](https://huggingface.co/RecursiveSI/flint-nvfp4-gguf)

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""The Flint split-KV decode attention kernel must match an fp64 reference at
+bf16 output-rounding level, mirror FlashInfer trtllm-gen's numerics, and stay
+correct under CUDA graph replay with new sequence lengths."""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+
+if not current_platform.is_cuda() or not current_platform.is_device_capability_family(
+    100
+):
+    pytest.skip("Flint decode attention targets SM100", allow_module_level=True)
+
+from flashinfer.decode import trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache  # noqa: E402
+
+from vllm.models.flint.ops.decode_attention import flint_decode_attention  # noqa: E402
+
+HQ, HKV, D, PAGE = 32, 4, 128, 16
+SCALE = D**-0.5
+WINDOW = 513
+
+
+def _make(
+    seq_lens: list[int], seed: int = 0
+) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    """Random q/K/V/sinks; blocks are shuffled so block tables are non-trivial."""
+    g = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(seed)
+    pages = [(s + PAGE - 1) // PAGE for s in seq_lens]
+    num_blocks = sum(pages) + 5
+    kv = torch.randn(num_blocks, HKV, PAGE, 2 * D, device="cuda", generator=g)
+    perm = torch.randperm(num_blocks, device="cuda", generator=g).int()
+    bt = torch.zeros(len(seq_lens), max(pages + [1]) + 2, dtype=torch.int32)
+    bt = bt.cuda()
+    o = 0
+    for i, n in enumerate(pages):
+        bt[i, :n] = perm[o : o + n]
+        o += n
+    q = torch.randn(len(seq_lens), HQ, D, device="cuda", generator=g) * 2
+    sinks = torch.randn(HQ, device="cuda", generator=g) * 2
+    sl = torch.tensor(seq_lens, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+    return q.bfloat16(), kv.bfloat16(), bt, sl, sinks
+
+
+def _reference(q, kv, bt, seq_lens, sinks, window):
+    out = torch.zeros(q.shape, dtype=torch.float64, device=q.device)
+    for i, s in enumerate(seq_lens.tolist()):
+        if s == 0:
+            continue
+        n = (s + PAGE - 1) // PAGE
+        x = kv[bt[i, :n].long()].permute(1, 0, 2, 3).reshape(HKV, n * PAGE, 2 * D)
+        x = x[:, max(s - window, 0) if window else 0 : s].double()
+        k, v = x[..., :D], x[..., D:]
+        scores = torch.einsum("hgd,htd->hgt", q[i].double().view(HKV, -1, D), k)
+        scores = scores * SCALE
+        sink = sinks.double().view(HKV, -1, 1)
+        m = torch.maximum(scores.amax(-1, keepdim=True), sink)
+        p = torch.exp(scores - m)
+        denom = p.sum(-1, keepdim=True) + torch.exp(sink - m)
+        out[i] = (torch.einsum("hgt,htd->hgd", p, v) / denom).reshape(HQ, D)
+    return out
+
+
+def _flashinfer(q, kv, bt, seq_lens, sinks, window):
+    workspace = torch.zeros(128 << 20, dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda")
+    k_cache, v_cache = kv.split(D, dim=-1)
+    return trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache(
+        q,
+        (k_cache, v_cache),
+        workspace,
+        bt,
+        seq_lens,
+        int(seq_lens.max()),
+        bmm1_scale=SCALE,
+        window_left=window - 1 if window else -1,
+        sinks=sinks,
+        kv_layout="HND",
+        backend="trtllm-gen",
+    )
+
+
+def _flint(q, kv, bt, seq_lens, sinks, window, out=None):
+    out = torch.empty_like(q) if out is None else out
+    return flint_decode_attention(q, kv, bt, seq_lens, sinks, window, SCALE, out)
+
+
+def _rel_err(x, ref):
+    """|x - ref| relative to each output row's max magnitude."""
+    scale = ref.abs().amax(-1, keepdim=True).clamp_min(1e-6)
+    return (x.double() - ref).abs() / scale
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "seq_lens",
+    [
+        [1],
+        [17],
+        [1000],
+        [20011],
+        [5, 77, 1000, 4097, 16, 33, 513, 3001],
+        [100, 2000, 37] * 10 + [1, 9000],
+    ],
+    ids=["1", "17", "1000", "20011", "mixed8", "mixed32"],
+)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("window", [None, WINDOW], ids=["full", "swa"])
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def test_matches_reference_and_flashinfer(seq_lens: list[int], window: int | None):
+    args = _make(seq_lens)
+    ref = _reference(*args, window)
+    out = _flint(*args, window)
+    fi_err = _rel_err(_flashinfer(*args, window), ref)
+    err = _rel_err(out, ref)
+    # One bf16 ulp of the row max is 2^-8; trtllm-gen also rounds its split
+    # partials to bf16, so its error bounds ours.
+    assert err.max() < 8e-3
+    assert err.max() <= fi_err.max() + 1e-3
+    assert err.mean() <= fi_err.mean() + 1e-4
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("seq_len", [513, 514, 529, 530, 545, 20000])
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def test_window_crosses_block_boundary(seq_len: int):
+    """The first attended page is partial; earlier tokens must be masked."""
+    args = _make([seq_len, seq_len + 7], seed=seq_len)
+    err = _rel_err(_flint(*args, WINDOW), _reference(*args, WINDOW))
+    assert err.max() < 8e-3
+
+
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def test_launch_from_another_stream_waits_for_the_previous_one():
+    """Launches share the split workspace and arrival counters, so a launch
+    from a different stream must not start before the previous one ends."""
+    args = _make([20011] * 4)
+    _flint(*args, None)
+    stream_a, stream_b = torch.cuda.Stream(), torch.cuda.Stream()
+    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+    with torch.cuda.stream(stream_a):
+        torch.cuda._sleep(100_000_000)  # ~50 ms at ~2 GHz
+        a_done = torch.cuda.Event()
+        _flint(*args, None)
+        a_done.record()
+    with torch.cuda.stream(stream_b):
+        _flint(*args, None)
+        b_done = torch.cuda.Event()
+        b_done.record()
+    b_done.synchronize()
+    assert a_done.query()
+
+
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def test_empty_request_writes_zeros():
+    q, kv, bt, sl, sinks = _make([0, 40])
+    out = torch.full_like(q, float("nan"))
+    _flint(q, kv, bt, sl, sinks, None, out)
+    assert (out[0] == 0).all()
+    assert _rel_err(out[1:], _reference(q, kv, bt, sl, sinks, None)[1:]).max() < 8e-3
+
+
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def test_probabilities_summed_in_fp32():
+    """Like trtllm-gen, P is rounded to bf16 for P @ V but the softmax
+    denominator sums the fp32 probabilities. With V = 1, one max-logit token
+    per page (so every split sees the same running max) and all other
+    probabilities just below a bf16 rounding midpoint, the output is visibly
+    below 1 (it would be exactly 1 with fp32 P or a bf16-P denominator)."""
+    n = 1000
+    q, kv, bt, sl, sinks = _make([n])
+    kv.zero_()
+    q.zero_()
+    q[..., 0] = 1.0
+    q[..., 1] = 2**-6
+    flat = kv.view(-1, HKV, PAGE, 2 * D)[bt[0, : (n + PAGE - 1) // PAGE].long()]
+    flat[..., 0] = -7.8125  # p = exp2((s - 0) * scale * log2e) = 0.50195..
+    flat[..., 1] = 0.9296875
+    flat[:, :, 0, :2] = 0.0  # first token of every page at the max (p = 1)
+    flat[..., D:] = 1.0
+    kv.view(-1, HKV, PAGE, 2 * D)[bt[0, : (n + PAGE - 1) // PAGE].long()] = flat
+    sinks.fill_(-100.0)
+    out = _flint(q, kv, bt, sl, sinks, None)
+    expected = _flashinfer(q, kv, bt, sl, sinks, None)
+    assert (expected == 0.99609375).all()
+    torch.testing.assert_close(out, expected, atol=0, rtol=0)
+
+
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def test_cuda_graph_replay_with_new_lengths():
+    """Grid shape depends only on the batch size; the split-combine counters
+    reset themselves, so replays with different lengths stay correct."""
+    lens_a = [30000, 17, 4100, 515]
+    lens_b = [1, 31000, 513, 9000]
+    q, kv, bt, sl, sinks = _make(lens_b)
+    out = torch.empty_like(q)
+    _, _, bt_a, sl_a, _ = _make(lens_a)
+    bt_a = torch.nn.functional.pad(bt_a, (0, bt.shape[1] - bt_a.shape[1]))
+    static_bt, static_sl = bt_a.clone(), sl_a.clone()
+    for window in (None, WINDOW):
+        _flint(q, kv, static_bt, static_sl, sinks, window, out)  # warm up / compile
+        graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+        with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
+            _flint(q, kv, static_bt, static_sl, sinks, window, out)
+        for bt_x, sl_x in ((bt, sl), (bt_a, sl_a), (bt, sl)):
+            static_bt.copy_(bt_x)
+            static_sl.copy_(sl_x)
+            graph.replay()
+            ref = _reference(q, kv, static_bt, static_sl, sinks, window)
+            assert _rel_err(out, ref).max() < 8e-3
+
+
+def _early_trigger_writer():
+    """A PDL kernel that releases its dependents immediately, idles ~2 us,
+    then writes one token's K/V into the cache, like
+    ``qk_norm_rope_cache(launch_dependents=True)``."""
+    import cutlass
+    import cutlass.cute as cute
+    from cutlass import Int32, Int64
+
+    class Writer:
+        @cute.jit
+        def __call__(self, src, dst, cycles: Int32, stream):
+            self.kernel(src, dst, cycles).launch(
+                grid=(1, 1, 1), block=(256, 1, 1), stream=stream, use_pdl=True
+            )
+
+        @cute.kernel
+        def kernel(self, src, dst, cycles: Int32):
+            cute.arch.griddepcontrol_wait()
+            cute.arch.griddepcontrol_launch_dependents()
+            t0 = cute.arch.clock64()
+            while cute.arch.clock64() - t0 < Int64(cycles):
+                pass
+            tid, _, _ = cute.arch.thread_idx()
+            dst[tid] = src[tid]
+
+    from cutlass.cute.runtime import make_fake_stream
+    from quack.compile_utils import make_fake_tensor
+
+    bf16 = cutlass.BFloat16
+    return cute.compile(
+        Writer(),
+        make_fake_tensor(bf16, (256,), divisibility=8),
+        make_fake_tensor(bf16, (256,), divisibility=8),
+        Int32(1),
+        make_fake_stream(use_tvm_ffi_env_stream=True),
+        options="--enable-tvm-ffi",
+    )
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("window", [None, WINDOW], ids=["full", "swa"])
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def test_current_token_written_by_pdl_predecessor(window: int | None):
+    """K/V pages are prefetched before the grid-dependency wait, except the
+    page holding the current token: K/V written there by an early-triggering
+    predecessor must be seen."""
+    writer = _early_trigger_writer()
+    # The last write (request 3, head 3) races the attention kernel; with one
+    # token, a stale read would change that output entirely.
+    lens = [20011, 4096, 17, 1]
+    q, kv, bt, sl, sinks = _make(lens)

+reference rounding rule on both the decode (GEMV) and the grouped-GEMM paths
+and route exactly like sigmoid top-k."""

+def _nvfp4(rows: int, cols: int, gen: torch.Generator):
+    w = torch.randint(
+        0, 256, (E, rows, cols // 2), dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda", generator=gen
+    )
+    # E4M3 scales over ~2^-6..2^2 with all mantissas.
+    exp = torch.randint(1, 10, (E, rows, cols // 16), device="cuda", generator=gen)
+    man = torch.randint(0, 8, (E, rows, cols // 16), device="cuda", generator=gen)
+    s = ((exp << 3) | man).to(torch.uint8).view(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
+    gs = torch.rand(E, device="cuda", generator=gen) * 2e-3 + 1e-3
+    return w, s, gs
+

+    router = (torch.randn(E, H, device="cuda", generator=gen) * 0.02).bfloat16()
+    return dict(w13=w13, s13=s13, gs13=gs13, w2=w2, s2=s2, gs2=gs2, router=router)

+def _inputs(num_tokens: int, seed: int | None = None):
+    gen = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(
+        num_tokens if seed is None else seed
+    )
+    x = torch.randn(num_tokens, H, device="cuda", generator=gen)
+    x = (x * torch.rsqrt(x.pow(2).mean(-1, keepdim=True))).bfloat16()
+    shared = (torch.randn(num_tokens, H, device="cuda", generator=gen) * 0.1).bfloat16()
+    return x, shared

+def _reference(x, w, ids, tw, shared, bf16_points: bool):
+    """MoE on exactly dequantized weights with fp32 GEMMs.
+
+    bf16_points=False: everything in fp32 (returns fp32).
+    bf16_points=True: the reference (TRTLLM MoE) rounding rule (returns bf16):
+    fp32 gate/up, act = bf16(silu(g) * u), y_e = bf16(acc_e * global_scale_e),
+    routed = bf16(sum_e tw_e * y_e) in fp32 (tw already bf16-rounded by the
+    router), out = bf16(routed + shared).
+    """
+    bf = torch.bfloat16
+    routed = torch.zeros(x.shape[0], H, device=x.device)
+    for e in ids.unique().tolist():
+        tok, slot = (ids == e).nonzero(as_tuple=True)
+        w13 = dequantize_nvfp4(w["w13"][e], w["s13"][e], torch.tensor(1.0))
+        w2 = dequantize_nvfp4(w["w2"][e], w["s2"][e], torch.tensor(1.0))
+        gu = (x[tok].float() @ w13.T) * w["gs13"][e]
+        g, u = gu[:, :INTER], gu[:, INTER:]
+        if bf16_points:
+            h = (torch.nn.functional.silu(g) * u).to(bf).float()
+            y = ((h @ w2.T) * w["gs2"][e]).to(bf).float()
+        else:
+            h = torch.nn.functional.silu(g) * u
+            y = (h @ w2.T) * w["gs2"][e]
+        routed.index_add_(0, tok, tw[tok, slot, None] * y)
+    if not bf16_points:
+        return routed + shared.float()
+    return (routed.to(bf).float() + shared.float()).to(bf)
+
+
+def _rel(a: torch.Tensor, b: torch.Tensor) -> float:
+    return float((a.float() - b.float()).norm() / b.float().norm())
+
+
+def _run(x, router, fw, shared, decode_max: int | None = None):
+    """flint_moe with an optionally forced decode/grouped dispatch."""
+    old = moe.DECODE_MAX_TOKENS
+    if decode_max is not None:
+        moe.DECODE_MAX_TOKENS = decode_max
+    try:
+        counter = moe.make_route_counter("cuda")
+        return moe.flint_moe(x, router, fw, TOPK, counter, shared)
+    finally:
+        moe.DECODE_MAX_TOKENS = old

+@torch.inference_mode()
+def test_dequant_exact():
+    """The E2M1 * E4M3 decode is exact for every (code, scale) pair."""
+    import triton
+    import triton.language as tl
+
+    @triton.jit
+    def kernel(w_ptr, s_ptr, out_ptr, N: tl.constexpr):
+        offs = tl.arange(0, N)
+        o = moe._dequant8(tl.load(w_ptr + offs), tl.load(s_ptr + offs))
+        for j in tl.static_range(8):
+            tl.store(out_ptr + offs * 8 + j, o[j])
+
+    # Every non-NaN E4M3 scale applied to one 16-code block holding codes
+    # 0..15 (two int32 words).
+    scales = torch.arange(256, dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda")
+    scales = scales[(scales & 0x7F) != 0x7F]
+    codes = torch.arange(16, dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda")
+    block = codes[0::2] | (codes[1::2] << 4)
+    words = block.repeat(scales.numel()).view(torch.int32)
+    n = words.numel()
+    padded_w = torch.zeros(512, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+    padded_s = torch.zeros(512, dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda")
+    padded_w[:n] = words
+    padded_s[:n] = scales.repeat_interleave(2)
+    out_dtype = torch.bfloat16 if moe._DEQUANT_BF16 else torch.float16
+    padded_out = torch.empty(512 * 8, dtype=out_dtype, device="cuda")
+    kernel[(1,)](padded_w, padded_s, padded_out, N=512)
+    ref = dequantize_nvfp4(
+        block.repeat(scales.numel()).view(-1, 8),
+        scales.view(torch.float8_e4m3fn).view(-1, 1),
+        torch.tensor(1.0),
+    )
+    torch.testing.assert_close(
+        padded_out[: n * 8].float(), ref.flatten(), rtol=0, atol=0
+    )
+

+def test_routing(weights, num_tokens: int):
+    x, _ = _inputs(num_tokens)
+    counter = moe.make_route_counter("cuda")
+    ids, tw = moe.route(x, weights["router"], TOPK, counter)
+    if num_tokens > moe.ROUTE_GEMV_MAX_TOKENS:
+        # Same cuBLAS bf16 GEMM as the kernel path; only top-k is under test.
+        logits = (x @ weights["router"].T).float()
+    else:
+        logits = (x.float() @ weights["router"].float().T).bfloat16().float()
+    ref_s, ref_ids = torch.sigmoid(logits).topk(TOPK, dim=-1)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(
+        ids.sort(-1).values, ref_ids.int().sort(-1).values, rtol=0, atol=0
+    )
+    # Renormalized as the reference does, then rounded to bf16.
+    ref_tw = ref_s / (ref_s.sum(-1, keepdim=True) + 1e-20)
+    ref_tw = ref_tw.bfloat16().float()
+    order, ref_order = ids.argsort(-1), ref_ids.argsort(-1)
+    got, ref_tw = tw.gather(1, order), ref_tw.gather(1, ref_order)
+    # The fp32 sigmoid / sum may differ in the last bit: rare 1-ulp bf16 flips.
+    assert (got == ref_tw).float().mean() > 0.99
+    torch.testing.assert_close(got, ref_tw, rtol=2**-7, atol=0)

+"""Flint's dense-linear and elementwise ops against high-precision references:
+the small-M NVFP4 / BF16 GEMVs (``nvfp4_gemv``, incl. the fused SiLU-and-mul
+epilogue), the large-M dequantize + cuBLAS path and global-scale check
+(``linear``), and the Triton norms and SiLU-and-mul (``norm``)."""

+import torch
+
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.nvfp4_utils import (
+    swizzle_blockscale,
+)
+from vllm.models.flint.gguf_nvfp4 import dequantize_nvfp4
+from vllm.models.flint.ops import nvfp4_gemv
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(
+    not current_platform.is_device_capability_family(100),
+    reason="SM100 only",
+)
+
+
+def _cases(table):
+    """(N, K, M) for each tuned shape: M within the first token tile, and a
+    partial and a full largest tile."""
+    return [
+        (n, k, m)
+        for (n, k), cfgs in table.items()
+        for m in sorted({1, 5, 8 * max(cfgs) - 3, 8 * max(cfgs)})
+    ]
+
+
+def _nvfp4(n: int, k: int, seed: int = 0):
+    gen = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(seed)
+    w = torch.randint(
+        0, 256, (n, k // 2), dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda", generator=gen
+    )
+    # Every finite non-negative E4M3 code, subnormals and zero included.
+    s = torch.randint(
+        0, 127, (n, k // 16), dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda", generator=gen
+    ).view(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
+    gs = torch.tensor(1.7e-3, device="cuda")
+    return w, s, gs
+
+
+def _reference(x, w, s, gs):
+    return x.double() @ dequantize_nvfp4(w, s, gs).double().t()
+
+
+def _silu_and_mul_ref(gate_up):
+    g, u = gate_up.float().chunk(2, dim=-1)
+    return (g / (1 + torch.exp(-g)) * u).bfloat16()
+
+
+def _check(out, ref):
+    # FP32 accumulation over K <= 6144 terms vs. a float64 reference: far
+    # below one BF16 ulp, so the only visible error is the output rounding.
+    err = (out.double() - ref).abs()
+    tol = 2.0**-8 * ref.abs() + 1e-3 * ref.abs().max()
+    assert (err <= tol).all(), f"max err {err.max().item()}"
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("n,k,m", _cases(nvfp4_gemv._TUNED))
+def test_gemv_matches_dequantized_reference(n, k, m):
+    w, s, gs = _nvfp4(n, k)
+    x = torch.randn(m, k, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+    out = nvfp4_gemv.nvfp4_gemv(x, w, swizzle_blockscale(s), gs)
+    _check(out, _reference(x, w, s, gs))
+
+
+def test_gemv_dequantizes_every_code_exactly():
+    """A one-hot activation reads back single dequantized weights bit-exactly:
+    all 16 E2M1 codes times all finite E4M3 scales, incl. subnormals."""
+    n, k = 2048, 4096
+    w = torch.arange(256, dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda").repeat(n, k // 512)
+    w = w[torch.randperm(n, device="cuda")]
+    s = (torch.arange(n * k // 16, device="cuda") % 127).to(torch.uint8)
+    s = s.reshape(n, k // 16).view(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
+    gs = torch.tensor(1.7e-3, device="cuda")
+    m = 16
+    x = torch.zeros(m, k, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+    x[torch.arange(m), torch.randint(0, k, (m,))] = 1.0
+    out = nvfp4_gemv.nvfp4_gemv(x, w, swizzle_blockscale(s), gs)
+    ref = (x.float() @ dequantize_nvfp4(w, s, gs).t()).bfloat16()
+    torch.testing.assert_close(out, ref, rtol=0, atol=0)
+
+
+def test_gemv_strided_input():
+    n, k = 2048, 4096
+    w, s, gs = _nvfp4(n, k)
+    base = torch.randn(4, k + 256, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+    x = base[:, 128 : 128 + k]
+    out = nvfp4_gemv.nvfp4_gemv(x, w, swizzle_blockscale(s), gs)
+    _check(out, _reference(x, w, s, gs))
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("n,k,m", _cases(nvfp4_gemv._TUNED_SILU_MUL))
+def test_gemv_silu_mul_matches_unfused(n, k, m):
+    """The fused gate_up + SiLU-and-mul epilogue equals SiLU-and-mul applied to
+    the BF16-rounded GEMM output."""
+    w, s, _ = _nvfp4(n, k)
+    gs = torch.tensor(1e-5, device="cuda")  # gate/up values of O(1-10)
+    gen = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(m)
+    x = torch.randn(m, k, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda", generator=gen)
+    ref = _silu_and_mul_ref(_reference(x, w, s, gs).bfloat16())
+    out = nvfp4_gemv.nvfp4_gemv(x, w, swizzle_blockscale(s), gs, silu_mul=True)
+    # FP32 vs float64 sums can round a gate/up value one BF16 ulp apart, which
+    # SiLU amplifies for negative gates (~3% at -8).
+    err = (out.float() - ref.float()).abs()
+    close = err <= 2**-7 * ref.float().abs() + 1e-6
+    assert close.float().mean() > 0.999
+    assert (err <= 0.1 * ref.float().abs() + 1e-5).all()
+
+
+def test_merged_global_scale_mismatch_raises():
+    from vllm.models.flint.ops.linear import check_merged_global_scales
+
+    p = "model.layers.0.self_attn."
+    ok = [(f"{p}{n}_proj.weight_scale_2", torch.tensor(0.5)) for n in "qkv"]
+    assert len(list(check_merged_global_scales(ok))) == 3
+    bad = ok[:2] + [(p + "v_proj.weight_scale_2", torch.tensor(0.25))]
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
+        list(check_merged_global_scales(bad))
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("n,k,m", _cases(nvfp4_gemv._TUNED_BF16))
+def test_bf16_gemv_matches_reference(n, k, m):
+    w = torch.randn(n, k, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+    x = torch.randn(m, k, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+    out = nvfp4_gemv.bf16_gemv(x, w)
+    _check(out, x.double() @ w.double().t())
+
+
+def test_bf16_gemv_silu_mul():
+    n, k = 2048, 2048
+    gen = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(0)
+    w = torch.randn(n, k, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda", generator=gen) * 0.05
+    x = torch.randn(4, k, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda", generator=gen)
+    ref = _silu_and_mul_ref((x.double() @ w.double().t()).bfloat16())
+    out = nvfp4_gemv.bf16_gemv(x, w, silu_mul=True)
+    err = (out.float() - ref.float()).abs()
+    assert (err <= 2**-7 * ref.float().abs() + 1e-6).float().mean() > 0.999
+
+
+def test_large_m_dequant_gemm_matches_reference():
+    from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+    from vllm.models.flint.ops.linear import _dequant_gemm
+
+    n, k = 2048, 4096
+    w, s, gs = _nvfp4(n, k)
+    layer = SimpleNamespace(
+        weight=w,
+        flint_weight_scale=swizzle_blockscale(s),
+        flint_global_scale=float(gs),
+    )
+    x = torch.randn(256, k, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+    _check(_dequant_gemm(layer, x), _reference(x, w, s, gs))
+
+
+def _rms_norm_ref(s, w, eps):
+    rs = torch.rsqrt(s.pow(2).mean(-1, keepdim=True) + eps)
+    return (s * rs * w.float()).bfloat16()
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("m", [1, 7, 8192])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("has_residual", [False, True])
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def test_rms_norm_matches_reference(m, has_residual):
+    """Flint's (fused residual-add) RMSNorm: fp32 math on the unrounded
+    x + residual, one bf16 rounding of each output. rsqrt.approx and the
+    reduction order allow rare 1-ulp differences from the fp32 reference."""
+    from vllm.models.flint.ops import norm
+
+    gen = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(m)
+    h = 2048
+    x = (torch.randn(m, h, device="cuda", generator=gen) * 2).bfloat16()
+    w = torch.empty(h, device="cuda").normal_(1, 0.2, generator=gen).bfloat16()
+    if has_residual:
+        r = (torch.randn(m, h, device="cuda", generator=gen) * 4).bfloat16()
+        s = x.float() + r.float()
+        out, res_out = norm.fused_add_rms_norm(x.clone(), r.clone(), w, 1e-6)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(res_out, s.bfloat16(), rtol=0, atol=0)
+    else:
+        out = norm.rms_norm(x, w, 1e-6)
+        s = x.float()
+    ref = _rms_norm_ref(s, w, 1e-6)
+    assert (out == ref).float().mean() > 0.999
+    torch.testing.assert_close(out, ref, rtol=2**-7, atol=0)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("m", [1, 7, 8192])
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def test_silu_and_mul_matches_reference(m):
+    """bf16(silu(g) * u) in fp32 with one rounding."""
+    from vllm.models.flint.ops import norm
+
+    gen = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(m)
+    x = (torch.randn(m, 2 * 6144, device="cuda", generator=gen) * 3).bfloat16()
+    out = norm.silu_and_mul(x)
+    ref = _silu_and_mul_ref(x)
+    assert (out == ref).float().mean() > 0.999
+    torch.testing.assert_close(out, ref, rtol=2**-7, atol=1e-6)

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

+"""Flint's NVFP4 GGUF loader must repack llama.cpp NVFP4 blocks into the
+ModelOpt layout without changing any weight value."""
+
+import numpy as np
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm.models.flint import gguf_nvfp4
+from vllm.models.flint.gguf_nvfp4 import (
+    _repack_nvfp4,
+    dequantize_nvfp4,
+    find_gguf_file,
+    gguf_nvfp4_weights_iterator,
+)
+
+gguf = pytest.importorskip("gguf", minversion="0.19.0")
+
+NVFP4 = gguf.GGMLQuantizationType.NVFP4
+
+
+def _random_blocks(rows: int, cols: int, seed: int = 0) -> np.ndarray:
+    # Random bytes cover every E2M1 code and every representable scale byte,
+    # including the sign bit and the 0x7F NaN pattern that ggml decodes as 0.
+    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
+    blocks = rng.integers(0, 256, (rows, cols // 64, 36), dtype=np.uint8)
+    blocks[..., :4] = np.where(blocks[..., :4] == 0xFF, 0x7F, blocks[..., :4])
+    return blocks.reshape(rows, -1)
+
+
+def test_repack_matches_gguf_dequantize():
+    rows, cols = 32, 512
+    blocks = _random_blocks(rows, cols)
+    weight, weight_scale = _repack_nvfp4(torch.from_numpy(blocks), cols)
+    assert weight.shape == (rows, cols // 2)
+    assert weight_scale.shape == (rows, cols // 16)
+    ours = dequantize_nvfp4(weight, weight_scale)
+    ref = gguf.quants.dequantize(blocks, NVFP4).reshape(rows, cols)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(ours, torch.from_numpy(ref), atol=0, rtol=0)
+
+
+def test_unrepresentable_scale_raises():
+    blocks = _random_blocks(1, 64)
+    blocks[0, 0] = 0xFF
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
+        _repack_nvfp4(torch.from_numpy(blocks), 64)
+
+
+def test_iterator_maps_names_and_scales(tmp_path):
+    hidden, inter, vocab, experts = 128, 64, 256, 4
+    path = tmp_path / "tiny.gguf"
+    writer = gguf.GGUFWriter(str(path), "flint")
+
+    def add_nvfp4(name, rows, cols, num, seed):
+        blocks = _random_blocks(num * rows, cols, seed).reshape(num, rows, -1)
+        data = blocks[0] if num == 1 else blocks
+        writer.add_tensor(name + ".weight", data, raw_dtype=NVFP4)
+        scale = np.full((num,), 0.5, dtype=np.float32) * np.arange(1, num + 1)
+        writer.add_tensor(name + ".scale", scale)
+        return data
+
+    q = add_nvfp4("blk.2.attn_q", hidden, hidden, 1, 1)
+    add_nvfp4("blk.2.ffn_up_exps", inter, hidden, experts, 2)
+    head = add_nvfp4("output", vocab, hidden, 1, 3)
+    writer.add_tensor("blk.2.attn_sinks.weight", np.zeros(4, dtype=np.float32))
+    writer.write_header_to_file()
+    writer.write_kv_data_to_file()
+    writer.write_tensors_to_file()
+    writer.close()
+
+    tensors = dict(
+        gguf_nvfp4_weights_iterator(str(path), "cpu", frozenset({"lm_head"}))
+    )
+
+    q_w = tensors["model.layers.2.self_attn.q_proj.weight"]
+    q_s = tensors["model.layers.2.self_attn.q_proj.weight_scale"]
+    assert q_w.dtype == torch.uint8 and q_s.dtype == torch.float8_e4m3fn
+    ref = gguf.quants.dequantize(q, NVFP4).reshape(hidden, hidden) * 0.5
+    torch.testing.assert_close(
+        dequantize_nvfp4(
+            q_w, q_s, tensors["model.layers.2.self_attn.q_proj.weight_scale_2"]
+        ),
+        torch.from_numpy(ref),
+        atol=0,
+        rtol=0,
+    )
+    # Stacked experts are split per expert with their own global scale.
+    for e in range(experts):
+        gs = tensors[f"model.layers.2.mlp.experts.{e}.up_proj.weight_scale_2"]
+        assert float(gs) == 0.5 * (e + 1)
+    # The LM head is dequantized exactly to bf16 (global scale kept apart).
+    head_w = tensors["lm_head.weight"]
+    assert head_w.dtype == torch.bfloat16
+    head_ref = gguf.quants.dequantize(head, NVFP4).reshape(vocab, hidden)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(
+        head_w.float(), torch.from_numpy(head_ref), atol=0, rtol=0
+    )
+    assert float(tensors["lm_head.weight_scale_2"]) == 0.5
+    assert "model.layers.2.self_attn.softmax_offset" in tensors
+
+
+def test_find_gguf_file_resolves_hub_repo_ids(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
+    """`vllm serve <org>/<repo>` must detect a GGUF-only repo, not just local paths."""
+    (tmp_path / "flint.gguf").touch()
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        gguf_nvfp4,
+        "any_pattern_in_repo_files",
+        lambda repo, patterns, revision: repo == "org/gguf",
+    )
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        gguf_nvfp4, "download_weights_from_hf", lambda *args: str(tmp_path)
+    )
+    assert find_gguf_file("org/gguf") == str(tmp_path / "flint.gguf")
+    assert find_gguf_file("org/safetensors") is None

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""The fused q/k norm + RoPE + cache-write kernel must reproduce the unfused
+vLLM ops (rms_norm, rotary_embedding, reshape_and_cache_flash) it replaces."""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm import _custom_ops as ops
+from vllm.models.flint.ops.qk_norm_rope import qk_norm_rope_cache
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+
+HQ, HKV, D = 32, 4, 128
+BLOCK_SIZE, NUM_BLOCKS = 16, 64
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(not current_platform.is_cuda(), reason="CUDA only")
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("num_tokens", [1, 7, 256, 1000])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("apply_rope", [True, False])
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def test_matches_unfused_ops(num_tokens: int, apply_rope: bool):
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    dev = "cuda"
+    qkv = torch.randn(num_tokens, (HQ + 2 * HKV) * D, device=dev).bfloat16() * 3
+    positions = torch.randint(0, 100_000, (num_tokens,), device=dev)
+    q_w = torch.empty(D, device=dev).normal_(1.0, 0.2).bfloat16()
+    k_w = torch.empty(D, device=dev).normal_(1.0, 0.2).bfloat16()
+    inv_freq = 1.0 / (10000.0 ** (torch.arange(0, D, 2, device=dev).float() / D))
+    freqs = torch.outer(torch.arange(262144, device=dev).float(), inv_freq)
+    cos_sin = torch.cat([freqs.cos(), freqs.sin()], dim=-1)
+    # Padded tokens (beyond the slot mapping) and slot -1 must not be written.
+    slots = torch.randperm(NUM_BLOCKS * BLOCK_SIZE, device=dev)[:num_tokens]
+    slot_mapping = slots[: max(1, num_tokens - 1)].clone()
+    slot_mapping[0] = -1
+
+    q, k, v = qkv.split([HQ * D, HKV * D, HKV * D], dim=-1)
+    ref_q = torch.empty(num_tokens, HQ, D, device=dev, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    ref_k = torch.empty(num_tokens, HKV, D, device=dev, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    ops.rms_norm(ref_q, q.reshape(-1, HQ, D), q_w, 1e-6)
+    ops.rms_norm(ref_k, k.reshape(-1, HKV, D), k_w, 1e-6)
+    ref_q = ref_q.reshape(q.shape)
+    ref_k = ref_k.reshape(k.shape)
+    if apply_rope:
+        # fp32 cos/sin with bf16 q/k, as in the reference implementation.
+        ops.rotary_embedding(positions, ref_q, ref_k, D, cos_sin, True)
+    ref_cache = torch.zeros(NUM_BLOCKS, 2, BLOCK_SIZE, HKV, D, device=dev).bfloat16()
+    torch.ops._C_cache_ops.reshape_and_cache_flash(
+        ref_k.reshape(-1, HKV, D),
+        v.reshape(-1, HKV, D),
+        ref_cache[:, 0],
+        ref_cache[:, 1],
+        slot_mapping,
+        "auto",
+        torch.ones((), device=dev),
+        torch.ones((), device=dev),
+    )
+
+    cache = torch.zeros_like(ref_cache)
+    out_qkv = qkv.clone()
+    out_q = qk_norm_rope_cache(
+        out_qkv,
+        positions,
+        q_w,
+        k_w,
+        1e-6,
+        cos_sin if apply_rope else None,
+        cache[:, 0],
+        cache[:, 1],
+        slot_mapping,
+        HQ,
+        HKV,
+        D,
+    )
+    out_k = out_qkv[:, HQ * D : (HQ + HKV) * D]
+    # Same ops and roundings; only the RMS reduction order differs.
+    torch.testing.assert_close(out_q, ref_q, atol=4e-3, rtol=1.6e-2)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(out_k, ref_k, atol=4e-3, rtol=1.6e-2)
+    assert (out_q != ref_q).float().mean() < 0.01
+    assert (out_k != ref_k).float().mean() < 0.01
+    torch.testing.assert_close(cache, ref_cache, atol=4e-3, rtol=1.6e-2)
+    assert torch.equal(out_qkv[:, (HQ + HKV) * D :], v)

+"""The two-kernel fused decode qkv (residual-add RMSNorm, then qkv GEMV with
+per-head q/k norm, RoPE and KV-cache write) must reproduce the kernels it
+replaces, Flint's ``fused_add_rms_norm`` / ``rms_norm`` -> Flint GEMV ->
+``qk_norm_rope_cache``, up to reduction order (rare 1-ulp differences)."""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+
+if not current_platform.is_cuda() or not current_platform.is_device_capability_family(
+    100
+):
+    pytest.skip("Flint fused qkv targets SM100", allow_module_level=True)
+
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.nvfp4_utils import (  # noqa: E402
+    swizzle_blockscale,
+)
+from vllm.models.flint.ops import norm, nvfp4_gemv  # noqa: E402
+from vllm.models.flint.ops.qk_norm_rope import qk_norm_rope_cache  # noqa: E402
+from vllm.models.flint.ops.qkv_fused import flint_qkv_fused  # noqa: E402
+
+HQ, HKV, D, K = 32, 4, 128, 2048
+N = (HQ + 2 * HKV) * D
+NUM_BLOCKS, BLOCK_SIZE = 64, 16
+
+
+def _weights(bf16w: bool, g: torch.Generator):
+    if bf16w:
+        w = (torch.randn(N, K, device="cuda", generator=g) * 0.02).bfloat16()
+        return w, None, None
+    w = torch.randint(0, 256, (N, K // 2), device="cuda", generator=g)
+    scales = torch.rand(N, K // 16, device="cuda", generator=g) * 2 + 0.25
+    scales = swizzle_blockscale(scales.to(torch.float8_e4m3fn))
+    return w.to(torch.uint8), scales, torch.tensor([0.0037], device="cuda")
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("m", [1, 2, 5, 8])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("bf16w", [False, True], ids=["nvfp4", "bf16"])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "has_residual,rope",
+    [(True, True), (True, False), (False, True), (False, False)],
+    ids=["res-rope", "res-norope", "first-layer", "first-norope"],
+)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("short_slots", [False, True], ids=["pad", "short"])
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def test_matches_unfused_kernels(
+    m: int, bf16w: bool, has_residual: bool, rope: bool, short_slots: bool
+):
+    g = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(m)
+    w, ws, gs = _weights(bf16w, g)
+    x = (torch.randn(m, K, device="cuda", generator=g) * 3).bfloat16()
+    res = None
+    if has_residual:
+        res = (torch.randn(m, K, device="cuda", generator=g) * 3).bfloat16()
+    norm_w = torch.empty(K, device="cuda").normal_(1, 0.2, generator=g).bfloat16()
+    q_w = torch.empty(D, device="cuda").normal_(1, 0.2, generator=g).bfloat16()
+    k_w = torch.empty(D, device="cuda").normal_(1, 0.2, generator=g).bfloat16()
+    cos_sin = None
+    if rope:
+        inv = 1.0 / (10000.0 ** (torch.arange(0, D, 2, device="cuda").float() / D))
+        freqs = torch.outer(torch.arange(262144, device="cuda").float(), inv)
+        # FP32 cos | sin table, as get_rope(..., dtype=torch.float32) builds.
+        cos_sin = torch.cat([freqs.cos(), freqs.sin()], dim=-1)
+    # Up to the end of the RoPE table.
+    positions = torch.randint(262144 - 64, 262144, (m,), device="cuda", generator=g)
+    slots = torch.randperm(NUM_BLOCKS * BLOCK_SIZE, device="cuda", generator=g)[:m]
+    # Padding tokens are skipped: a -1 slot, or beyond a shorter slot mapping.
+    if m > 1 and short_slots:
+        slots = slots[:-1]
+    elif m > 1:
+        slots[-1] = -1
+    kv = torch.zeros(
+        NUM_BLOCKS, HKV, BLOCK_SIZE, 2 * D, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16
+    )
+    ref_kv = kv.clone()
+
+    if res is not None:
+        xr, ref_res = norm.fused_add_rms_norm(x.clone(), res.clone(), norm_w, 1e-6)
+    else:
+        xr = norm.rms_norm(x, norm_w, 1e-6)
+    if bf16w:
+        qkv = (xr.float() @ w.float().t()).bfloat16()
+    else:
+        qkv = nvfp4_gemv.nvfp4_gemv(xr, w, ws, gs)
+    ref_k, ref_v = ref_kv.transpose(1, 2).split(D, dim=-1)
+    ref_q = qk_norm_rope_cache(
+        qkv, positions, q_w, k_w, 1e-6, cos_sin, ref_k, ref_v, slots, HQ, HKV, D
+    )
+
+    k_cache, v_cache = kv.transpose(1, 2).split(D, dim=-1)
+    q, res_out = flint_qkv_fused(
+        x, res, norm_w, 1e-6, w, ws, gs, q_w, k_w, 1e-6, cos_sin, positions,
+        k_cache, v_cache, slots, HQ, HKV,
+    )  # fmt: skip
+
+    if has_residual:
+        torch.testing.assert_close(res_out, ref_res, atol=0, rtol=0)
+    else:
+        assert res_out is x
+    # Same rounding points, but the norms (and the BF16 GEMV's K split) sum in
+    # a different fp32 order: a 1-ulp difference in a normalized activation
+    # shifts every qkv output of its token slightly.
+    assert (q == ref_q).float().mean() > 0.9
+    assert (kv == ref_kv).float().mean() > 0.9
+    torch.testing.assert_close(q, ref_q, atol=1e-2, rtol=2e-2)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(kv, ref_kv, atol=1e-2, rtol=2e-2)

+from typing import Any

+from transformers.configuration_utils import PreTrainedConfig

+class FlintConfig(PreTrainedConfig):
+    """Decoder-only MoE transformer with hybrid sliding/full attention.
+
+    Sliding layers use RoPE; full-attention layers listed in
+    ``no_rope_layer_indices`` use no positional encoding. Every attention head
+    has a learned sink logit. ``sliding_window`` counts the current token.
+    """
+
+    model_type = "flint"
+    keys_to_ignore_at_inference = ["past_key_values"]
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        vocab_size: int = 150144,
+        hidden_size: int = 2048,
+        intermediate_size: int = 6144,
+        num_hidden_layers: int = 49,
+        num_attention_heads: int = 32,
+        num_key_value_heads: int = 4,
+        head_dim: int = 128,
+        hidden_act: str = "silu",
+        max_position_embeddings: int = 262144,
+        initializer_range: float = 0.02,
+        rms_norm_eps: float = 1e-6,
+        use_cache: bool = True,
+        tie_word_embeddings: bool = False,
+        rope_theta: float = 10000.0,
+        rope_parameters: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
+        attention_bias: bool = False,
+        attention_dropout: float = 0.0,
+        use_sliding_window: bool = True,
+        sliding_window: int | None = 513,
+        layer_types: list[str] | None = None,
+        no_rope_layer_indices: list[int] | None = None,
+        moe_intermediate_size: int = 512,
+        shared_expert_intermediate_size: int = 1024,
+        num_experts_per_tok: int = 6,
+        num_experts: int = 256,
+        norm_topk_prob: bool = True,
+        router_score_function: str = "sigmoid",
+        mlp_only_layers: list[int] | None = None,
+        **kwargs,
+    ):
+        self.vocab_size = vocab_size
+        self.hidden_size = hidden_size
+        self.intermediate_size = intermediate_size
+        self.num_hidden_layers = num_hidden_layers
+        self.num_attention_heads = num_attention_heads
+        self.num_key_value_heads = num_key_value_heads
+        self.head_dim = head_dim
+        self.hidden_act = hidden_act
+        self.max_position_embeddings = max_position_embeddings
+        self.initializer_range = initializer_range
+        self.rms_norm_eps = rms_norm_eps
+        self.use_cache = use_cache
+        self.rope_theta = rope_theta
+        self.rope_parameters = rope_parameters or {
+            "rope_type": "default",
+            "rope_theta": rope_theta,
+        }
+        self.attention_bias = attention_bias
+        self.attention_dropout = attention_dropout
+        self.use_sliding_window = use_sliding_window
+        self.sliding_window = sliding_window if use_sliding_window else None
+        self.layer_types = layer_types or ["full_attention"] * num_hidden_layers
+        if len(self.layer_types) != num_hidden_layers:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"layer_types has {len(self.layer_types)} entries but "
+                f"num_hidden_layers is {num_hidden_layers}"
+            )
+        self.no_rope_layer_indices = no_rope_layer_indices or []
+        self.moe_intermediate_size = moe_intermediate_size
+        self.shared_expert_intermediate_size = shared_expert_intermediate_size
+        self.num_experts_per_tok = num_experts_per_tok
+        self.num_experts = num_experts
+        self.norm_topk_prob = norm_topk_prob
+        self.router_score_function = router_score_function
+        self.mlp_only_layers = mlp_only_layers or []
+        # The reference implementation computes the LM head in fp32.

+

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Load Flint's NVFP4 GGUF checkpoint as ModelOpt-layout NVFP4 tensors.
+
+A GGUF NVFP4 super-block holds 64 values as four 16-value sub-blocks, each with
+a UE4M3 scale byte and 8 bytes of E2M1 codes (low nibbles = values 0..7, high
+nibbles = values 8..15). The value is ``e4m3(scale) * e2m1(code) * tensor_scale``
+where ``tensor_scale`` is the companion ``<name>.scale`` F32 tensor (one per
+expert for stacked expert tensors). ModelOpt packs consecutive values into one
+byte (low nibble first) and stores the same three factors as ``weight``,
+``weight_scale`` and ``weight_scale_2``, so conversion is a lossless repack.
+"""
+
+import glob
+import os
+import warnings
+from collections.abc import Iterator
+
+import huggingface_hub
+import numpy as np
+import regex as re
+import torch
+
+from vllm.model_executor.model_loader.weight_utils import download_weights_from_hf
+from vllm.transformers_utils.repo_utils import any_pattern_in_repo_files
+
+_GGUF_NVFP4 = 40
+_QK = 64
+_BLOCK_BYTES = 36
+
+_LAYER_NAMES = {
+    "attn_norm.weight": "input_layernorm.weight",
+    "ffn_norm.weight": "post_attention_layernorm.weight",
+    "attn_q_norm.weight": "self_attn.q_norm.weight",
+    "attn_k_norm.weight": "self_attn.k_norm.weight",
+    "attn_sinks.weight": "self_attn.softmax_offset",
+    "attn_q": "self_attn.q_proj",
+    "attn_k": "self_attn.k_proj",
+    "attn_v": "self_attn.v_proj",
+    "attn_output": "self_attn.o_proj",
+    "ffn_gate": "mlp.gate_proj",
+    "ffn_up": "mlp.up_proj",
+    "ffn_down": "mlp.down_proj",
+    "ffn_gate_shexp": "mlp.shared_expert.gate_proj",
+    "ffn_up_shexp": "mlp.shared_expert.up_proj",
+    "ffn_down_shexp": "mlp.shared_expert.down_proj",
+    "ffn_gate_inp.weight": "mlp.gate.weight",
+}
+_EXPERT_NAMES = {
+    "ffn_gate_exps": "gate_proj",
+    "ffn_up_exps": "up_proj",
+    "ffn_down_exps": "down_proj",
+}
+_GLOBAL_NAMES = {
+    "token_embd.weight": "model.embed_tokens.weight",
+    "output_norm.weight": "model.norm.weight",
+    "output": "lm_head",
+}
+
+
+def find_gguf_file(
+    model_path: str, revision: str | None = None, download_dir: str | None = None
+) -> str | None:
+    if os.path.isfile(model_path) and model_path.endswith(".gguf"):
+        return model_path
+    if not os.path.isdir(model_path):
+        # Offline, the repo cannot be listed; look in the cached snapshot instead.
+        offline = huggingface_hub.constants.HF_HUB_OFFLINE
+        if not offline and not any_pattern_in_repo_files(
+            model_path, ["*.gguf"], revision=revision
+        ):
+            return None
+        try:
+            model_path = download_weights_from_hf(
+                model_path, download_dir, ["*.gguf"], revision
+            )
+        except huggingface_hub.errors.LocalEntryNotFoundError:
+            return None
+    files = sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(model_path, "*.gguf")))
+    if len(files) > 1:
+        raise ValueError(f"Expected one GGUF file in {model_path}, found {files}")
+    return files[0] if files else None
+
+
+def _repack_nvfp4(
+    blocks: torch.Tensor, n_cols: int
+) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    """[..., n_cols / 64 * 36] GGUF bytes -> (packed [..., n_cols / 2] uint8,
+    block scales [..., n_cols / 16] float8_e4m3fn)."""
+    lead = blocks.shape[:-1]
+    blocks = blocks.reshape(*lead, n_cols // _QK, _BLOCK_BYTES)
+    # ggml decodes the scales as unsigned E4M3 and the NaN pattern as zero;
+    # 0xFF would decode to 480, which E4M3 cannot represent.
+    scales = blocks[..., :4]
+    if bool((scales == 0xFF).any()):
+        raise ValueError("NVFP4 GGUF block scale 0xFF is not supported")
+    scales = torch.where(scales == 0x7F, torch.zeros_like(scales), scales & 0x7F)
+    qs = blocks[..., 4:].reshape(*lead, n_cols // _QK, 4, 8)
+    codes = torch.cat([qs & 0x0F, qs >> 4], dim=-1)
+    packed = codes[..., 0::2] | (codes[..., 1::2] << 4)
+    return (
+        packed.reshape(*lead, n_cols // 2).contiguous(),
+        scales.reshape(*lead, n_cols // 16).contiguous().view(torch.float8_e4m3fn),
+    )
+
+
+_E2M1_POS = (0.0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0, 6.0)
+_E2M1 = _E2M1_POS + tuple(-v for v in _E2M1_POS)
+
+
+def dequantize_nvfp4(
+    weight: torch.Tensor,
+    weight_scale: torch.Tensor,
+    global_scale: torch.Tensor | None = None,
+    out_dtype: torch.dtype = torch.float32,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """ModelOpt-layout NVFP4 [N, K / 2] -> [N, K]. Without ``global_scale`` the
+    result is ``e2m1 * e4m3``, which is exact in bf16."""
+    chunk_rows = 8192
+    lut = torch.tensor(_E2M1, dtype=torch.float32, device=weight.device)
+    out = torch.empty(
+        (*weight.shape[:-1], weight.shape[-1] * 2),
+        dtype=out_dtype,
+        device=weight.device,
+    )
+    for start in range(0, weight.shape[0], chunk_rows):
+        w = weight[start : start + chunk_rows]
+        codes = torch.stack([w & 0x0F, w >> 4], dim=-1).int()
+        values = lut[codes].reshape(*w.shape[:-1], -1, 16)
+        values = values * weight_scale[start : start + chunk_rows].float().unsqueeze(-1)
+        values = values.flatten(-2)
+        if global_scale is not None:
+            values = values * global_scale.float().to(weight.device)
+        out[start : start + chunk_rows] = values
+    return out
+
+
+def _as_tensor(data: np.ndarray) -> torch.Tensor:
+    # The reader memory-maps the file read-only; tensors are only read.
+    with warnings.catch_warnings():
+        warnings.simplefilter("ignore", UserWarning)
+        return torch.from_numpy(np.asarray(data))
+
+
+def _map_name(name: str) -> tuple[str, bool]:
+    """GGUF tensor base name -> (HF base name, is_stacked_experts)."""
+    if name in _GLOBAL_NAMES:
+        return _GLOBAL_NAMES[name], False
+    m = re.fullmatch(r"blk\.(\d+)\.(.+)", name)
+    if m is None:
+        raise ValueError(f"Unexpected tensor in Flint GGUF: {name}")
+    layer, rest = m.groups()
+    prefix = f"model.layers.{layer}."
+    if rest in _EXPERT_NAMES:
+        return prefix + "mlp.experts.{}." + _EXPERT_NAMES[rest], True
+    if rest not in _LAYER_NAMES:
+        raise ValueError(f"Unexpected tensor in Flint GGUF: {name}")
+    return prefix + _LAYER_NAMES[rest], False
+
+
+def gguf_nvfp4_weights_iterator(
+    path: str,
+    device: torch.device | str = "cuda",
+    dequantize: frozenset[str] = frozenset(),
+) -> Iterator[tuple[str, torch.Tensor]]:
+    """Yield HF-style (name, tensor) pairs; NVFP4 tensors become ``.weight``
+    (packed uint8), ``.weight_scale`` (E4M3) and ``.weight_scale_2`` (F32),
+    except HF base names in ``dequantize``, which become a BF16 ``.weight``
+    holding ``e2m1 * e4m3`` (exact) plus the F32 ``.weight_scale_2`` that the
+    caller applies to the fp32 output."""
+    try:
+        import gguf
+    except ImportError as err:
+        raise ImportError(
+            "Loading Flint NVFP4 GGUF checkpoints requires the `gguf` package "
+            "(pip install 'gguf>=0.19.0')."
+        ) from err
+
+    reader = gguf.GGUFReader(path)
+    prec_a4 = reader.fields.get("general.tensor_extra.prec_a4")
+    if prec_a4 is not None and any(prec_a4.contents()):
+        raise ValueError(
+            "GGUF marks tensors with FP4 activations (prec_a4); only weight-only "
+            "NVFP4 (W4A16) is supported."
+        )
+    tensors = {t.name: t for t in reader.tensors}
+    for name, t in tensors.items():
+        if name.endswith(".scale"):
+            continue
+        data = _as_tensor(t.data)
+        if t.tensor_type != _GGUF_NVFP4:
+            hf_name, _ = _map_name(name)
+            if t.tensor_type == gguf.GGMLQuantizationType.BF16:
+                data = data.view(torch.bfloat16)
+            elif t.tensor_type != gguf.GGMLQuantizationType.F32:
+                raise ValueError(
+                    f"Unsupported GGUF tensor type for {name}: {t.tensor_type}"
+                )
+            yield hf_name, data
+            continue
+
+        base = name.removesuffix(".weight")
+        hf_base, stacked = _map_name(base)
+        n_cols = int(t.shape[0])
+        weight, weight_scale = _repack_nvfp4(data.to(device), n_cols)
+        global_scale = _as_tensor(tensors[base + ".scale"].data)
+        if hf_base in dequantize:
+            yield (
+                hf_base + ".weight",
+                dequantize_nvfp4(weight, weight_scale, out_dtype=torch.bfloat16),
+            )
+            yield hf_base + ".weight_scale_2", global_scale.reshape(())
+            continue
+        if not stacked:
+            yield hf_base + ".weight", weight
+            yield hf_base + ".weight_scale", weight_scale
+            yield hf_base + ".weight_scale_2", global_scale.reshape(())
+            continue
+        for e in range(weight.shape[0]):
+            expert = hf_base.format(e)
+            yield expert + ".weight", weight[e]
+            yield expert + ".weight_scale", weight_scale[e]
+            yield expert + ".weight_scale_2", global_scale[e]

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
